about: Dated official recall data (cluster K12, C94). Rows come from the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's own recall notices (cpsc.gov), read on the checked date; each row carries the CPSC recall number, the recall date, the source URL and the checked date. Matching runs against the person's own purchases (packages/domain/118-found-money.js and the earn engine's E3 found money): the product, not only the store — a purchase confirms a recall only when its record names the product. A remedy is claimed with the manufacturer or agency exactly as the notice states; Upmore prepares the claim, the owner submits it. Re-check monthly; past fresh_days a row is said to may have changed.

recalls.checked_how: CPSC recall notice 26-780 (Fast Track Recall, announced September 17, 2026): about 84,000 units, sold exclusively at Target stores and Target.com from July 2025 through August 2026 for about $30; date codes OET 25100, OET 25150 or OET 26064 on the packaging identify recalled units.
recalls.hazard: The fire hose port can come loose and detach, posing a risk of serious injury from a choking hazard. Stop using it and keep it away from children.
recalls.product: Melissa & Doug Lights & Sounds Fire Truck Activity Board
recalls.remedy: Register on Melissa & Doug's recall page, then choose: a free replacement fire truck activity board, a refund of the $30 purchase price by check, or a $40 credit at melissaanddoug.com. Registration asks you to remove the batteries, write RECALL and a unique code on the front, cut off the black hose, and upload a photo before disposing of the toy.

recalls.checked_how: CPSC recall notice 26-778 (announced September 17, 2026): about 195,000 heated blankets and heating pads, sold only on Amazon.com from September 2022 through July 2026, in one-packs and two-packs.
recalls.hazard: The internal wire heating elements can overheat, creating fire and burn hazards (577 reports of smoking, melting or burning, including 53 burn injuries). Stop using it and unplug it.
recalls.remedy: A full refund of the purchase price from JKMAX. Contact JKMAX through its recall site or by email at JkmaxRecall@outlook.com; Amazon also lists it under Recalls and Product Safety Alerts. The model number is on the back of the detachable remote or on the packaging label.
